proof_language.name: CUTTING_PLANES
proof_language.lines: integer linear inequalities over Boolean variables

relation_to_resolution.witness_family: pigeonhole principle has polynomial-size CP refutations while requiring exponential-size Resolution refutations

theorem_used.title: Automating Cutting Planes is NP-Hard
theorem_used.statement_used: Given an unsatisfiable CNF F, it is NP-hard to find a dag-like Cutting Planes refutation in time polynomial in the length of a shortest CP refutation of F.
theorem_used.conditional_form: If dag-like Cutting Planes were polynomial-time automatable in the standard shortest-proof sense, then P=NP.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: Replacing Resolution by the strictly stronger Cutting Planes proof language does not provide an easier route to L3 uniform polynomial proof discovery.
reason: CP genuinely escapes some Resolution proof-size lower bounds because CP polynomially simulates Resolution and is exponentially stronger on known families.
Nevertheless, unrestricted CP proof search is NP-hard to automate.
Therefore SHORT_CP_PROOF_EXISTS cannot be promoted to POLYTIME_CP_PROOF_DISCOVERY.
A universal TRUMP L3 constructor whose proof-search core is standard CP automatization would already cross the P=NP frontier rather than discharge an easier intermediate obligation.
derived_TRUMP_barrier.scope: This is a proof-search barrier for standard dag-like Cutting Planes automatization. It does not prove that every proof system stronger than CP is non-automatable, and it does not prove P!=NP.

next_rule: Any next proof language must again be fixed exactly and receive either a polynomial-discovery theorem or a proof-search hardness theorem; proof-size simulation alone is insufficient.
